chunks: Too glorious is your Lord, the Lord of power, for what they ascribe to Him.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is glorious from what they ascribe to Him?
ai.summary: In the context of Surah As-Saffat, this verse serves as the divine response to the angels' inquiry about the nature of the Messiah, clarifying that God is far above the anthropomorphic or familial attributes ascribed by polytheists. Shia exegesis highlights this as a cornerstone of Tawhid al-Asma wa al-Sifat, affirming God's transcendence (Tanzih) from physical limitations and human-like qualities. It underscores the purity of the Divine Essence against the misconceptions of those who project human characteristics onto the Creator.
